components.css: .ds-folio { width:240px; padding:12px; border-right:1px solid var(--color-line,#cbd5e3); background:linear-gradient(90deg,rgba(174,191,215,.26),transparent 42%),var(--color-surface-1,#eaf0f6); font-family:var(--font-sans,Outfit,sans-serif); } .ds-folio-mark { display:block; padding:8px 10px 14px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--color-line,#cbd5e3); color:var(--color-ink-4,#5e6b85); font-family:var(--font-mono,monospace); font-size:9px; letter-spacing:.12em; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-folio-item { position:relative; display:flex; align-items:center; gap:10px; min-height:34px; padding:0 10px; border-radius:var(--radius-sm,6px); color:var(--color-ink-2,#394968); font-size:13px; text-decoration:none; } .ds-folio-item small { margin-left:auto; color:var(--color-ink-4,#5e6b85); font-family:var(--font-mono,monospace); font-size:10px; } .ds-folio-item:hover { background:rgba(251,249,244,.7); color:var(--color-ink,#25345a); } .ds-folio-item.is-active { background:var(--color-ember-tint,rgba(174,191,215,.26)); color:var(--color-ink,#25345a); font-weight:600; } .ds-folio-item.is-active::before { content:''; position:absolute; left:4px; top:50%; width:6px; height:6px; background:var(--color-danger,#8e4657); transform:translateY(-50%) rotate(45deg); }

narrative.overview: CreativeForge should feel like a working atelier rather than a control panel: ivory work surfaces, mist-blue air, ink-blue typography, silver rules, and a few wax-red moments reserved for consequence. The visual world borrows the poise and ceremony of a rococo salon, but translates it into a production tool where the asset, the agent's reasoning, and the next action remain immediately legible.
keyCharacteristics: Paper and vellum surfaces with precise silver-blue rules.
Ink-blue type on warm ivory, with mist blue used as atmosphere rather than decoration.
One expressive opening sequence; routine product motion stays quiet.
Dossier-like secondary panels, ticket-like controls, and postmark-like metadata.
Dense work areas stay calm, rectangular, and scan-friendly.
Chinese typography is designed, not left to fallback.

rules.name: The Consequence Rule
rules.body: Wax red never decorates inactive content; it marks a decision, interruption, or irreversible action.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Paper Rule
rules.body: Body text and controls use ink blue on ivory or canvas, not gray on blue.

rules.name: The Chinese Voice Rule
rules.body: Latin display faces may set English and French accents, but Chinese display text always uses Noto Serif SC with its own weight and line-height tuning.

rules.name: The Label Rule
rules.body: Display and script faces never appear in buttons, form labels, table headers, or dense operational text.

dos: Use real product content and actual status vocabulary.
Pair every semantic color with text or shape.
Keep the center work area calm and concentrate decoration.
Test Chinese, English, mixed strings, long paths, and large numbers at every breakpoint.
donts: Copy Kimi Code branding, copy, or page content.
Put display fonts in operational labels.
Nest cards or add ornament to every panel.
Use blur, gradients, or texture as a substitute for hierarchy.
Let the opening animation block access when assets or routes fail.
